metadata.title: Infrastructure reliability incident investigation
metadata.artifact_scope_note: Evidence is aggregated query output (not raw log lines or metric samples); it contains no chat/communication records.

incident_description: Reliability incident investigation of a production environment. Evidence consists of Elasticsearch aggregation results over application and proxy logs, Kubernetes, cloud-provider and host system events, Prometheus Alertmanager alerts, change-management / CI-CD audit records and metric anomaly detection. No root cause, impact or trigger is stated; these must be established from the supplied artifacts. Environment context: Organization: Stratmark Clinics (clinic and patient management SaaS); Platform: on-premises data center DC-Central, server range 10.132.0.0/16; Kubernetes cluster stratm-prod (kubeadm); consent-svc pods run with 4 GiB memory limits; deployments are canary releases with automated analysis; Change management: production changes carry CHG- identifiers.
investigation_questions: Which account or automation identity executed the triggering change?
Which version of the service introduced the defect?
During what hour did the first signs of the failure appear? Provide the earliest date and time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC format.

What is the root cause category of the incident: configuration change, software defect, hardware failure, cloud provider failure, capacity exhaustion, automation error, certificate expiry, or third-party dependency failure?
Which of the three CIA components is primarily affected: availability, integrity, or confidentiality?
According to the error volume statistics, what single service emitted the most errors? Is it the root cause or a downstream symptom?
What change brought the service back to normal? Give its identifier.
